entities.span: A real engaged kill switch reaching `checkUsageGate()` end to end could not be a committed integration test at first, and the reason was structural rather than a one off flake to route around. `app_settings` is a single row by design (spec 0002), so no test can hold its own copy of it, and `checkUsageGate()` reads that same row on every call, from every integration file. Vitest schedules different integration files to run in parallel by default, so ANY committed test that flips the switch races every other file's concurrent gate calls, not just one specific assertion. Tried twice on 2026-09-03, once alongside `checkUsageGate()`'s own suite and once inside `kill-switch.test.ts` beside its own read of the row (same file placement does remove a race with that ONE read, since Vitest runs tasks within a file sequentially, confirmed against the installed `@vitest/runner` 4.1.11): both attempts broke `test/integration/usage-gating.test.ts`'s unrelated account week burst test, twice in three extra runs, because that test's calls landed while the switch was engaged in a different file. **Corrected 2026-09-03, same day, after a fresh model review** (`docs/reviews/2026-09-03-feat-usage-gating-kill-switch.md`) verified in Vitest 4.1.11's own shipped types that `sequence.groupOrder` exists and does what its doc comment says: a project set to a higher group order runs only after every lower numbered group has finished. `fileParallelism: false` was named here as "the only real fix"; that claim was wrong, and `groupOrder` is the cheaper one, since it isolates only the files that need it from `integration`'s own files rather than serialising every integration file for every file's sake. Implemented the same day: a third Vitest project, `integration-serial` (`test/integration-serial/`, `sequence.groupOrder: 1`), added to `vitest.config.mts` and to `test:integration` in `package.json`. **One more correction the same day**, found by actually running it rather than trusting the reasoning: `groupOrder` orders PROJECTS, not the files inside one, so Vitest still schedules multiple files within `integration-serial` in parallel with each other, the same default `integration` itself has. The real engaged switch and AC-14's database fault test were first split into two files there and immediately raced each other, the kill switch flip making the database fault test observe `kill_switch_engaged` instead of the `database_unavailable` it was testing for, the exact failure shape this whole change exists to prevent. Merged into one file, `test/integration-serial/shared-global-state.test.ts`, since tests within one file are the only ordering actually guaranteed (confirmed against the installed `@vitest/runner` 4.1.11's own task runner), proved race free across five consecutive full `pnpm test:integration` runs after the merge. Every future scenario needing this same real shared state belongs in that one file too, not a new one of its own. **Corrected again 2026-09-04, a third fresh model review**: "tests within one file are the only ordering actually guaranteed" stopped being the reason this is safe the same day, once `fileParallelism: false` was added to `integration-serial` as the mechanical backstop that review's first round flagged as missing (the one-file rule was prose only before that, since `include` matched any file dropped in, and a second one would have raced the first, the exact failure this project exists to prevent). `groupOrder` still isolates the project from `integration`; `fileParallelism` now serialises the files within it. The scenarios still belong in one file
